findings.location: Kerem Shalom goods crossing, Gaza Strip
findings.affected_population_system: Civilians reliant on humanitarian aid, food, fuel, shelter and medical supplies entering Gaza
findings.incident_summary: Newly surfaced Gaza-side crossing bulletin records 239 aid trucks (down from 305 the preceding week, -22%), 33 fuel tankers (down from 36) and 746 commercial-goods trucks, totaling 1,018 entries through Kerem Shalom during November 6–12. Kerem Shalom was open for goods five days, while Zikim and Kissufim were reported closed all seven days. This is a retrospective weekly access finding, not a change during the observation hour.

findings.location: Rafah, Kerem Shalom passenger crossings, Gaza Strip
findings.affected_population_system: Palestinian patients, companions and other people seeking movement out of or back into Gaza
findings.incident_summary: The Gaza-side bulletin newly made available via NCF reports 212 departures from Gaza (versus 295 a week earlier) and 159 returns (versus 242), with Rafah passenger crossing open 3 of 7 days. Its passenger category breakdown lists 96 patients, 113 companions and 3 evacuees; the report also labels three departures 'medical evacuations' without fully explaining the relationship to the 96 patient category. Avoid describing only three patients as evacuated. Retrospective November 6–12 data.
findings.exact_supporting_passage: 212 people left Gaza, down from 295 last week.

data.classification_caveat: The categories patients/companions/evacuees and the phrase medical evacuations are reported without sufficient definition for finer medical evacuation conclusions

Anadolu mentions Israeli fire toward homes and displacement tents along Al-Tina Street; no verified casualties, damaged structure or displacement consequence given, so no separate qualifying civilian-impact finding.
WAFA November 20 Gaza casualty report already logged by predecessor, not duplicated.
NCF roundup of November 10–19 incidents otherwise retells established events and was not counted as new incidents.
Search results for Gaza in November 2023–2025 excluded as year collisions; no fresh independently verified WHO health-system, detention, hostage or ceasefire agreement changes found.
limitations: WHO Eastern Mediterranean HTTP 502 persists; WHO global coverage remains available.
Gaza crossings bulletin was reported as obtained directly by NCF but its original PDF/official record was not independently retrieved; medium confidence, bounded single-source attribution.
The NCF passenger categories are not fully defined, especially three 'medical evacuations' alongside 96 listed patients.
Search indexes may lag or miss certain pages; no finding in a category does not prove no real incident occurred.
